Session 1 · 1983-01-01

I'm looking to replace a table lamp in my bedroom with a floor lamp. I just got one from IKEA, but I'm not sure what kind of bulb to use. I've had some issues with energy-efficient bulbs in the past, like the ones that are good for the environment, but I didn't like the blueish tint they gave off.

That's really helpful! I didn't know about the warm white vs cool white thing. I think I'll try out a warm white bulb to see if that works better for me. Do you have any recommendations for brands that offer bulbs with a warm white color temperature?

I'll check out some of those brands. I've got a Home Depot nearby, so I might check out their selection too. I had a good experience with their bulbs when I switched to warmer-toned ones in my living room.

Session 2 · 1983-06-09anchor #1

Polling day at last — I've been on my feet since half five this morning, knocking up in Hanley and getting my shoes soaked. Remind me to buy new insoles, these ones are done for.

Right, the count's at the town hall tonight. Can you hold my diary loose for tomorrow? I suspect I'll be running on tea and sandwiches and about two hours' sleep.

Well — it's done. The result came through and I'm now a member of the 49th Parliament of the United Kingdom, representing Stoke-on-Trent Central. Still slightly stunned, honestly. Someone handed me a warm glass of something and I lost my rosette in the crowd.

One last thing before I collapse: the car boot is still full of leaflets and a folding table, and I promised I'd return the loudhailer to the committee rooms. Nudge me about that later in the week, would you?

I'm based in the San Francisco Bay Area. I'd prefer a park or nature reserve within a 30-45 minute drive from the city center. We're a relatively active group, so a moderate trail with some scenic views would be perfect.

However, I\'m not sure if I should read it immediately or wait a bit since I\'ve just finished a historical fiction novel. Session 7 · 1985-11-15

I'm looking for some advice on aquarium plants. I just got some new ones in the mail and I want to make sure I'm giving them the best conditions to thrive. By the way, I just got rid of an algae bloom last weekend after weeks of battling it - had to do a big water change, scrub the glass, and adjust the lighting.

I got 3 types of plants - Anacharis, Java Moss, and Amazon Swords. My tank is a 20-gallon freshwater setup with a hang-on-back filter and a heater set to 76°F (24°C). As for water parameters, my pH is stable at 7.2, ammonia and nitrite are 0, and nitrate is around 10 ppm. I've also been monitoring the pH closely since I had a scare a few weeks ago when it dropped to 6.

I'm also thinking of getting some more fish to add to my school of harlequin rasboras. Do you have any recommendations for peaceful community fish that would do well with them?

I'm definitely going to try that recipe out this weekend. And I'm curious, do you have any suggestions for vegan-friendly restaurants in my neighborhood? I recently discovered one that I love, but it's always nice to have some options.

Session 10 · 1987-04-01

Session 11 · 1987-06-11anchor #2

Right, polling day at last — been up since half five handing out leaflets outside the school gates in Hanley and my feet are absolutely killing me. Remind me to buy new shoes before the next one.

Small mercy: Ingrid put a flask of tea and two cheese sandwiches in the car, so I've actually eaten something today. Can you note that I still need to ring the printers about the unpaid invoice for the last batch of posters — it's been sat on my desk a fortnight.

Well, the count's done and it went our way — so as of today I'm a member of the 50th Parliament of the United Kingdom again. Bit dazed, honestly. Half the committee room was singing and the other half was arguing about who'd left the urn on.

Diary bits before I collapse: thank-you notes to every last one of the volunteers (there were about forty), the car needs its oil looking at, and someone has to mow that lawn before it swallows the shed. Wake me at nine, not eight.

Jotting this down while it's fresh: ring Mum in the morning (she'll have stayed up, she always does), get the car back from outside the committee rooms, and somebody has to return the borrowed loudhailer to the ward office. Also we're out of milk at home, which feels like the real crisis.

Can you jot down that I promised the chap from the allotment association I'd ring him next week about the drainage business? He caught me on the way out and I nodded before I'd properly heard him.

Right, I'm going home for cheese on toast and about nine hours of sleep. Nothing before eleven tomorrow, please, and if anyone from the local paper calls, tell them I'll speak to them in the afternoon.

Session 36 · 2005-05-05anchor #6

Polling day, and naturally the rain has arrived exactly on schedule. Up at half five, rosette pinned on slightly crooked, and I've already eaten two of the biscuits that were meant for the tellers. Remind me to buy replacements before anyone notices.

Well — the votes are counted and it's official, I'm returned as member of the 54th Parliament of the United Kingdom. Ridiculous mixture of elation and wanting to sleep for a week. Please make a list of thank-you calls for tomorrow: the agent, the volunteers who did the knocking-up in the drizzle, and the lady at the church hall who kept everyone in tea.

One last thing before I collapse. The kitchen light bulb went last night and I keep forgetting — put it on the shopping list with milk and dog food. History-making evening, and I still can't see to make toast.

Session 1 · 1752-00-00anchor #1

Morning. The stove in my study smoked half the night again, so I slept badly and my back is complaining. Remind me to send for the chimney man before the week is out.

Big news to file away: I've been made titular archbishop, so the household is in a mild uproar and my sister has already written asking what she should wear. Note it down properly, with today's date.

Practical matters — I need a new pectoral cross chain (the old one's clasp is worn through), two pairs of black stockings, and the tailor must let out the shoulders on my winter cloak. Also the vintner from Litoměřice is coming Thursday and I refuse to be talked into another cask of that thin wine.

One more thing before I go to dinner: draft a short, warm letter of thanks to my cousin — he sent a very good cheese and a rather bad poem, so praise the cheese first and be vague about the verses.
